name: the players' waiting room inside the pyramid
about: The stone waiting room behind the arched Minpentai door, with elevator pods down to the arena (chapters 4 and 7). The book gives only the details listed below; the rest of the design is invented, and contributors are welcome to replace it.

facts.quote: Each corridor was about two meters wide, and three meters tall; the lower two meters were a rectangle, and the upper meter a semicircle.
a series of stone bricks, curving near the top into an arch
facts.fact: An arched door of stone bricks.

facts.quote: two horizontal arms, meeting in the middle with clashing fists
facts.fact: An emblem of two arms with clashing fists above the door.

facts.quote: Zei walked into one of the elevator pods on the wall.
facts.fact: Elevator pods set into the wall.

facts.quote: Two elevators opened up in the waiting room
facts.fact: The elevators open into the waiting room.

facts.quote: A robot slid toward them, and gave them three glasses of water.
You can watch last year's matches on that screen over there.
facts.fact: A screen for watching matches (capital waiting room).

descriptor: a windowless waiting room carved deep in a mountain, with polished pale stone walls and a vaulted round-topped ceiling, entered through an arch of stone bricks crowned by a carved emblem of two arms meeting with clashing fists, a row of sleek elevator pod doors set into one wall, low stone benches, a wall screen, a small serving robot, and warm indirect light
